entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a favorable belief or attitude as sufficient for behavior despite capability, opportunity, habits, or competing goals.
entities.definition: The degree to which a behavior-specific evaluation is confident, accessible, stable, and resistant to change.
entities.evidenceNotes: Scientifically defensible with substantial supporting literature, while causal identification, construct boundaries, measurement, or transferability remain context dependent. Representative records: SRC156; SRC117.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Validated construct-specific scales; structured belief elicitation; choice or expectancy tasks; repeated assessment
entities.measurementCaveats: Self-report may conflate evaluation, expectancy, and intention; behavior-specific wording and temporal alignment are essential.
entities.mechanism: Strong attitudes are retrieved more readily, guide interpretation, and resist counterpersuasion.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Behavioral specificity, direct experience, attitude accessibility, temporal stability, opportunity, and competing goals.
entities.name: Attitude Strength
entities.persistenceRecovery: Often persists for days to months; updating depends on counterevidence and confidence.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = stronger and more consequential attitude.
entities.representationScale: Composite of certainty, accessibility, importance, stability, and resistance

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a favorable belief or attitude as sufficient for behavior despite capability, opportunity, habits, or competing goals.
entities.definition: The degree to which performing a specified behavior is evaluated unfavorably or favorably.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC107; SRC110.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Validated construct-specific scales; structured belief elicitation; choice or expectancy tasks; repeated assessment
entities.measurementCaveats: Self-report may conflate evaluation, expectancy, and intention; behavior-specific wording and temporal alignment are essential.
entities.mechanism: Changes the subjective desirability of an option and contributes to intention and choice when accessible and relevant.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Behavioral specificity, direct experience, attitude accessibility, temporal stability, opportunity, and competing goals.
entities.name: Attitude Valence
entities.persistenceRecovery: Often persists for days to months; updating depends on counterevidence and confidence.
entities.polarityDirection: Negative values = unfavorable evaluation; positive values = favorable evaluation.
entities.representationScale: Validated semantic-differential or Likert composite anchored unfavorable–favorable

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a favorable belief or attitude as sufficient for behavior despite capability, opportunity, habits, or competing goals.
entities.definition: The degree of confidence or commitment attached to a specified proposition about the world.

entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Validated construct-specific scales; structured belief elicitation; choice or expectancy tasks; repeated assessment
entities.measurementCaveats: Self-report may conflate evaluation, expectancy, and intention; behavior-specific wording and temporal alignment are essential.
entities.mechanism: Weights the proposition more heavily in inference, prediction, and action selection.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Behavioral specificity, direct experience, attitude accessibility, temporal stability, opportunity, and competing goals.
entities.name: Belief Strength
entities.persistenceRecovery: Often persists for days to months; updating depends on counterevidence and confidence.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater confidence that the proposition is true.
entities.representationScale: 0–1 subjective probability or ordinal confidence scale

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a favorable belief or attitude as sufficient for behavior despite capability, opportunity, habits, or competing goals.
entities.definition: The judged likelihood that performing a specified action will produce a specified consequence.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC110; SRC111.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Validated construct-specific scales; structured belief elicitation; choice or expectancy tasks; repeated assessment
entities.measurementCaveats: Self-report may conflate evaluation, expectancy, and intention; behavior-specific wording and temporal alignment are essential.
entities.mechanism: Links action to anticipated consequences, altering expected value and action selection.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Behavioral specificity, direct experience, attitude accessibility, temporal stability, opportunity, and competing goals.
entities.name: Outcome Expectancy
entities.persistenceRecovery: Often persists for days to months; updating depends on counterevidence and confidence.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater expected likelihood of the specified consequence.

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a favorable belief or attitude as sufficient for behavior despite capability, opportunity, habits, or competing goals.
entities.definition: The subjective desirability or aversiveness assigned to a specified possible outcome.

entities.measurementCaveats: Self-report may conflate evaluation, expectancy, and intention; behavior-specific wording and temporal alignment are essential.

entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Behavioral specificity, direct experience, attitude accessibility, temporal stability, opportunity, and competing goals.

entities.polarityDirection: Negative values = aversive; positive values = desirable.
entities.representationScale: Negative–neutral–positive valuation; utility or willingness-to-pay measure

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a favorable belief or attitude as sufficient for behavior despite capability, opportunity, habits, or competing goals.

entities.measurementCaveats: Self-report may conflate evaluation, expectancy, and intention; behavior-specific wording and temporal alignment are essential.

relationships.conditionsModerators: Behavioral specificity, attitude strength, perceived control, habits, and temporal alignment
relationships.generalizabilityContext: Generalizability is limited to contexts compatible with the stated mechanism, conditions, and evidence.
relationships.mechanism: More favorable behavior-specific evaluation usually supports stronger intention, but the edge does not imply action.
relationships.notesCaveats: Migrated from v1 relationship type: Candidate causal influence. Legacy functional form: Generally monotonic but opportunity- and specificity-limited.

relationships.conditionsModerators: Valence, direct experience, accessibility, and opportunity
relationships.generalizabilityContext: Generalizability is limited to contexts compatible with the stated mechanism, conditions, and evidence.
relationships.mechanism: Stronger attitudes are generally more consequential for intention than weak or uncertain evaluations.
relationships.notesCaveats: Migrated from v1 relationship type: Moderating influence. Legacy functional form: Saturating. V2 review: legacy moderation label did not identify a separate governed edge; represented as a causal contribution at the stated resolution.
